1. Basic Information.Project Title: Knockout Tournament: Conversations over a Ping-pong Table

Year / Time Period.text: January 4-11, 2019, concurrent with the "Teer Art" art week

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This project was designed and executed concurrently with the "Teer Art" art week and functioned as a "Counter-event" against the dominant flow of the art market.

The initial idea was based on the symbolic confrontation between gallery-affiliated artists and independent artists, but subsequently, by opening participation to the public, the conventional hierarchical structures were challenged.
In this project, the game of ping-pong was not merely a sports competition, but transformed into a platform for "conversation in action."
After introducing themselves, participants would converse about their lived experiences, professional status, and working conditions during the game and between matches.
At the end of the tournament, Omid Fattahi (a massage therapist) won the championship, overcoming professional artists.
Second place went to Behzad Hatefi (a multimedia artist) and third place went to Morteza Darehbaghi (an abstract painter).
32 participants, comprising a wide spectrum of practitioners (painter, architect, curator, actor, massage therapist, etc.), attended this event.

sections.title: Context & Site
paragraphs: The interior space of "New Media Projects", through a temporary change of use, was transformed into an interactive sports space.

The space was designed in such a way that by eliminating classical exhibition arrangements, it removed the usual hierarchies (artist/audience or master/student) and placed everyone on the equal level of a "game."

sections.title: Motivations & Questions
paragraphs: The primary objective of the project was to establish fresh conversations and connections among the artistic community and to raise real issues of artistic life in an informal and non-hierarchical format.
The crisis of "livelihood and independence" was brought up as the central focus of the discussions.
It became evident during the discussions that the existence of an independent artist in the current ecosystem necessitates simultaneously assuming multiple, exhausting roles.
To survive, the artist is compelled to simultaneously take on the roles of creator, manager, accountant, marketer, and even the transporter of their own artworks.
This multifaceted pressure and the ensuing isolation underscored the necessity of creating a space for brainstorming, sharing experiences, and trade union solidarity.
Three major structural elements played a part in the formation of this event.

First was the critique of the "centralism" of events like "Teer Art," which had created a profound gap by exclusively focusing on the geography of Tehran and disregarding artists and curators from other provinces.

Second were the structural ambiguities in Iran's gallery system, particularly regarding vague contracts between galleries and artists (the distinction between displaying an artwork and exclusive representation) and the ineffectiveness of trade unions in resolving these issues.
Third was the critique of the educational system (from art conservatories to universities), which has deeply impacted the orientation and even the artistic taste of graduates.

sections.title: Constraints & Strategies
paragraphs: The main obstacles included mental and structural challenges in defining the artist's identity (the tension between independent artists and gallery-affiliated artists), as well as the physical limitations of the space to host a sports-art event.

The primary strategy involved "change of use" and "shifting concepts"; turning a sports competition into a critical and educational platform, and opening participation to the public to dismantle the hypothetical, elite-centric boundaries between artists and other societal classes.

sections.title: Fundings & Partners
paragraphs: Collaborators / Participating Institutions: -

Financial Sponsors: This project was organized completely independently, and its only financial source was the participants' entrance fee (20,000 Tomans), which was entirely spent on purchasing the symbolic championship cup.

sections.title: About the Artist
paragraphs: New Media Society was an independent, non-commercial, and research-oriented initiative in Tehran that began its activities in July 2014 (Tir 1393).
This center, functioning as an archive, library, and project space, focused on supporting media arts and fresh ideas.

The mission of this collective was pursued through organizing lectures, workshops, publishing texts, and cultural residency programs to fill the academic void while establishing a constructive connection between domestic and international artists.
New Media Society’s project space is closed as a physical space since Feb 2022 and at the moment the initiative is only active via its website / archive and the New Media Nomad School.
Website/Telegram: https://newmediasoc.com
There were 32 participants in this event, encompassing a wide range of practitioners: painter, architect, curator, actor, massage therapist, and other active individuals from various fields.

Audiences crossed the usual boundaries and were present in both the roles of "player" (active agent) and "spectator," actively participating in the discussions surrounding the economics and politics of art.

Discussions began with tracing the roots of the tendency toward abstract painting in the past decades and the influence of masters such as Nosratollah Kasraian and Yaghoub Amamehpich in the educational system, extending into topics concerning "performance and body studies."
During these discussions, theater acting techniques and body training for "making playing with an imaginary ball look real" were analyzed.
Additionally, the use of alternative objects (such as a paintbrush instead of a racket) as an executive metaphor demonstrated the existential condition of the artist within the field of art.
